detail:
verdict=deploy-ready; posted and transitioned; caveats:
  - The Mayo half of the change (MayoGetPatientInfoStrategy) was never executed: this instance logs 'Epic OAuth keys not configured - OAuth authentication disabled', so no Mayo patient-info fetch is possible and the Mayo call site was validated only by MGB exercising the same shared method.
  - FDB returns 403 Forbidden from this instance, so the flag-off fallback was confirmed to be taken (FDB screen request logged) but its real output could not be compared before and after.
  - Validation exercised the RxNorm-code-to-formulary-medication path this ticket delivers; the shipped AllergyAssociationService on main has since grown SNOMED and cross-reaction-group handling that was not the subject of this run.
  - The mgb-mgh mapping data maps rxnorm 2670 (codeine) to m-promethazine-oral, so a codeine allergy flags oral promethazine; the code faithfully applies the data but the mapping itself is worth a clinical eyeball.
  - Relaunching the same case appends duplicate patient_medication_allergies rows rather than replacing them; this affects the pre-existing antibiotic path identically and is not introduced by this change.
